headline: Samsung is raising prices for some advanced chip manufacturing by up to 15 percent because TSMC has no room left for new customers, Reuters reports.
score_reason: Shows the leading-edge chip shortage now feeding into prices; based on Reuters' unnamed sources, relayed second hand.
importance_line: Higher manufacturing prices flow through to the cost of AI processors and the devices built on them, affecting chip designers from Nvidia to Chinese firms who are being charged the most, though the figures rest on anonymous sources and Samsung has not confirmed them.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by Stocktwits, that Samsung is lifting prices on new orders for some of its advanced contract chipmaking services by as much as 15 percent, with Chinese customers facing the steepest rises, because rival TSMC is fully booked and Samsung is the only other foundry able to make 2-nanometre chips, the current leading edge. Sources told Reuters that Samsung is turning away some orders to keep capacity for US customers and its own chips, after already raising prices for its 4- and 5-nanometre processes in July.
notes: Stocktwits relays Reuters; Reuters is the source, original link not given, url is where the text was read. Reuters report date not stated in the copy; the premarket share move points to Friday 2 Oct. Score kept at 6 as the price rise itself is the news and could not be confirmed stale.
